market.summary: GIFT Nifty points to a firm open (about 26,050-26,100, roughly 1% above Wednesday's 25,819 close) and Asia is higher this morning. The new risk is trade: late last night the US proposed a Section 301 tariff of up to 25% on Indian goods (17% if a trade deal is signed), with health, steel, solar and ICT named as sectors of concern. US markets swung hard on a hot PCE print and an AI sell-off but ended mixed, and they are shut today for Thanksgiving, so there is no US lead tonight.

points.text: USTR proposed up to 25% on Indian goods under Section 301 (excess industrial capacity), cut to 17% with a trade deal; it replaces, not stacks on, the current 10%. India is one of 14 economies covered; reports say rates could start as early as January.

US, Wed 25 Nov: Dow +0.33% to 50,183 after being down over 1,100 points; S&P 500 -0.25%, Nasdaq -0.62% (Nvidia -3.9%); October PCE inflation 3.8%, Q3 GDP revised up to 4.3%; 10-year yield about 4.85%.
This morning: GIFT Nifty about 26,056 (+119), Nikkei +0.7%, Kospi +1.4%, US futures +0.5-0.6%; Brent January about $90.8 after attacks on a Saudi refinery; gold +0.9%.
Rupee rose 0.7% to 92.23 per dollar on Wednesday; foreign investors' November buying is reported at a record $14.3 billion.
NSE provisional flows, 25 Nov: FIIs bought a net Rs 4,479 Cr and DIIs Rs 4,019 Cr; FIIs have now been net buyers 11 sessions in a row.

market.watch: How the market takes the US tariff proposal after the gap-up open; small caps (DCI) lagged large caps yesterday.
